"The officers presented this booklet to the author with thankful appreciation and humbleness of spirit." A high point of interest was created in a review of the history of Savoy Male and Female College by its author, Miss Mattie Lee Boyd, daughter of a graduate ex-student, Pamelia Paxton (Mrs. P. F.) Boyd, which was compiled, written and submitted as a master's thesis in education to the University of the State of Texas. In recognition of her meritorious services the dedication of honorary membership in the Association was formally bestowed, and she was presented with No. 1 certificate of such membership in the Association.

Officers elected for the ensuing year were as follows: President, John Marcus Gist; vice-president, Edgar Anderson McMahon; secretary-treasurer, Martha Buford May; historian, Miss Mattie Lee Boyd; Board of Managers, Lee A. Clark, Lewis J. Reynolds and Guy P. Webb.

1940

The third reunion was held at Savoy, Sunday, June 16, 1940, with Vice-President Edgar Anderson McMahon presiding at the request of President John Marcus Gist, and Martha Buford May served as secretary.

The opening exercises consisted of "America," led by Mrs. Lewis J. Reynolds, of McKinney, with Mrs. Hugh L. A. Hamilton of Whitewright, as pianist, scripture reading by the Hon. B. Blaine Ragland, and a prayer by H. W. Alcorn of Dallas. An address of welcome was delivered by Honorable H. F. Bell, and a response made by John Marcus Gist of Sherman. A poem by the Association's Historian, Martha Buford May, titled "College Reunion Song" was sung. A roll call was then taken. Greetings were given by Mrs. W. H.1 Davis in her own inimical manner.
